claims: Video = function of time: frame(t) returns one picture, 60/sec, headless browser draws, FFmpeg stitches, sound is also a function of t
Claude can't watch video but can inspect frames/contact sheets and fix the function
Same prompt at low/high/ultracode effort: 20 min / 30 min / 8 hours; low and high 'did just fine', so quality is a prompt problem not an effort problem
Ask for a storyboard first to avoid hour-long regenerate loops
Reference video (made with Remotion) was recreated in JS with matching composition but different content
Entire pipeline is free beyond Claude usage; no AI video/image generator
how_to_steps: Level 1 prompt: state length, type (e.g. 30-second animated explainer), aspect ratio, 'in JavaScript on a canvas', soundtrack generated in code or supplied; ask for a storyboard of key frames before coding

Level 2 loop: 'Render it to an MP4 with Playwright and FFmpeg'; if you have narration: 'Here's my voice-over: voice.mp3. Time the visuals to it: get word timestamps with Whisper and land each change on the words'; end with 'Before you call it done, use FFmpeg to pull a contact sheet, look at it, fix what's wrong, re-render, and repeat'
Level 3 references: attach images to insert or copy aesthetic, or a video to copy composition; browse skillery.dev AI videos or 'Kevin' on Twitter for inspiration

Level 4 codify: install the creator's skill (plugin or URL); it runs intake (subject, format, audio/voice, hero character), story, look (2-4 style frames), storyboard (every beat), delivery (video + checks: cuts on the beat, loudest moment after the silence, narration pace); installs Playwright, FFmpeg, faster-whisper and offers the ElevenLabs connector
on_screen_only: Prompt text on screen: 'Make a 30-second animated explainer of how [TOPIC] works, 16:9. Build it in JavaScript on a canvas, with a soundtrack generated in code, and render it to an MP4 with Playwright and FFmpeg. Here's my voice-over: voice.mp3. Time the visuals to it: get word timestamps with Whisper and land each change on the words. Before you call it done, use FFmpeg to pull a contact sheet, look at it, fix what's wrong, re-render, and repeat.' with annotations 'Claude figures out the rest: renderFrame(t), the score, frame-by-frame rendering, encoding'
Test prompt: 'Make a dynamic 15 second motion graphics video that shows what an incredible motion designer you are, like it's a show reel for a resume. Go all out. Don't use any skills.'
Pipeline diagram: function frame(t) -> headless browser -> frames = 240 -> FFmpeg -> play; sound(t)
